events.title: Voltaire Is Born in Paris
events.description: François-Marie Arouet, who later took the pen name Voltaire, was born in Paris. He became one of the sharpest writers of the Enlightenment. His plays, essays, and satires targeted tyranny and religious intolerance.
events.significance: Voltaire's defense of free speech, tolerance, and reason helped shape modern ideas about civil liberties and influenced later revolutionary movements.

events.title: First Free Flight by Humans in a Hot-Air Balloon
events.description: Jean-François Pilâtre de Rozier and the Marquis d'Arlandes lifted off from Paris in a balloon built by the Montgolfier brothers. They floated over the city for about 25 minutes. They were the first people to fly without a tether.
events.significance: The flight showed that humans could rise into the sky and opened the era of aviation.

events.title: North Carolina Ratifies the U.S. Constitution
events.description: North Carolina became the 12th state to join the United States. It had earlier held back until a bill of rights was proposed.
events.significance: Its ratification brought the young republic close to full membership. Only Rhode Island remained outside the Union.

events.title: Edison Announces the Phonograph
events.description: Thomas Edison announced that he had invented the phonograph, a machine that could record sound and play it back. The news amazed the public and earned him the nickname 'the Wizard of Menlo Park.'
events.significance: Recorded sound launched the modern music and broadcasting industries and changed how people share and preserve voices and culture.

events.title: Emperor Franz Joseph I of Austria Dies
events.description: Franz Joseph I died at age 86. He had ruled the Habsburg Empire for almost 68 years, and his death came in the middle of World War I.
events.significance: His death ended one of the longest reigns in European history. The Austro-Hungarian Empire collapsed just two years later.
